newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Brittan says "would be crazy" to block telecom dea.
newsitem.headline: Brittan says "would be crazy" to block telecom dea.

text.p: EU Trade Commissioner Sir Leon Brittan said it "would be crazy" to abandon a global telecoms deal being negotiated in Geneva.

"What is on the table amounts to a massive liberalisation of the world telecommunication market that it would be crazy not to grab with both hands. I see no conceivable justification on the basis of what is on the table for failing to clinch the deal," he told reporters.
Brittan was speaking as negotiators expressed doubts that an accord could be reached by Saturday's deadline because of the tough U.S. line at the talks.

Earlier, Britain urged the United States to sign a global telecoms pact. "I would certainly urge the Americans to live up to their rhetoric...and sign up to an accord," British minister for science and technology, Ian Taylor, told a news briefing.
Taylor said he believed there was enough on the table for a deal.

U.S. officials declined to give a detailed assessment of the state of play, but they said their team to the World Trade Organisation negotiations insisted better offers were still needed from other countries.
